summary: This program defines a single growPlant method that takes sunlight and water as inputs, then reports whether the plant is growing based on those values. Instead of writing a separate method for every combination of conditions, one method handles them all through parameters.

lines.text: The two values in the parentheses are arguments: they are handed to the method and become its parameters for this one call. Changing them here changes the outcome without touching the method itself.

lines.text: The parameter list declares two named inputs with their types, so the method can work with any sunlight and water values a caller supplies.
Joining text to a boolean with + converts the boolean to the word "true" or "false" automatically, which is what makes this readable output.
The conditional operator picks one of two strings: if sunlight is true and water is at least 3, status becomes "Growing", otherwise "Needs care". It is a compact stand-in for a four-line if/else.
This reports the decision the method reached, so the caller can see the effect of the arguments it passed in.
